groups.name: Things that set off an asthma attack
groups.explanation: Each one can tighten twitchy asthmatic airways: hard exercise, a common painkiller, dirty air, and a viral infection.

article.text: Exercise: Breathing fast through the mouth dries and cools the airways, which can trigger exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.
Aspirin: Blocking COX shunts arachidonic acid toward leukotrienes, which squeeze the airways. This is aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (asthma, nasal polyps, aspirin sensitivity).
Air pollution: Ozone, smoke, and fine particles irritate the airway lining.
Influenza: Viral respiratory infections are among the most common causes of asthma flares.

groups.name: Lead poisoning
groups.explanation: One poison seen four ways: its treatment, a line on the gums, a speckled red cell, and what it does to a child's brain.

article.text: CaNa2EDTA: A chelator that binds lead so the kidneys can clear it. Severe cases add dimercaprol, and milder cases in children often get oral succimer.
Gum line: Burton lines, a blue-gray band of lead deposits along the gum margin.
Blood smear: Microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling. Lead blocks ferrochelatase and ALA dehydratase, so heme isn't made, and it leaves clumps of ribosomal RNA in the red cells.
Neurodevelopmental delay: Young children absorb lead easily, often from old paint, and it harms the developing brain.

groups.name: Causes of hemoptysis
groups.explanation: All four can make a patient cough up blood: scarred, widened airways, a lung fluke, an old cavity, and antibodies against basement membrane.

article.text: Chest CT: Bronchiectasis. Chronic infection and inflammation leave airways permanently widened, and their enlarged bronchial arteries bleed.
Wet mount: Paragonimus westermani, the lung fluke from undercooked crab or crayfish. Its operculated eggs show up in sputum or stool, and it can mimic TB.
Chest X-ray: Tuberculosis. Reactivation disease cavitates in the upper lobes and causes cough, night sweats, and hemoptysis.
Goodpasture syndrome: Anti-GBM antibodies attack type IV collagen in both the lungs and the kidneys, so it causes hemoptysis plus hematuria.

groups.name: Pathology described with cheese words
groups.explanation: Each one is described in textbooks with a cheese: Swiss cheese brain, cottage cheese discharge, cheesy (caseous) necrosis, and a Swiss cheese lung.

article.text: Brain MRI: Neurocysticercosis. Many small Taenia solium cysts give the brain a "Swiss cheese" look on CT or MRI.
Candidiasis: Thick, white, "cottage cheese" discharge with itching and a normal vaginal pH.
Caseous necrosis: The crumbly, white, cheese-like center of a TB or fungal granuloma. Caseus is Latin for cheese.
Emphysema: Destroyed alveolar walls leave enlarged air spaces, so the cut lung looks full of holes.

info.title: Exercise
info.text: Track clue: fast, cold, dry breathing during a hard run can tighten the airways a few minutes in.

info.title: Aspirin
info.text: Rx clue: a COX inhibitor. With COX blocked, more arachidonic acid goes to leukotrienes.

info.title: Air pollution
info.text: Weather clue: a smoggy, high-ozone day sends more patients to the ER wheezing.

info.title: Influenza
info.text: Virus clue: an enveloped RNA virus with hemagglutinin and neuraminidase spikes.

info.title: Calcium disodium EDTA
info.text: Rx clue: a chelating agent given by injection to pull a heavy metal out of the body.

info.title: Burton lines
info.text: Exam clue: a thin blue-gray line where the gums meet the teeth.

info.title: Basophilic stippling
info.text: Smear clue: small, pale red cells, one dotted with fine blue granules.

info.title: Neurodevelopmental delay
info.text: Peds clue: a toddler who is slow to talk, living in a house built before 1978.

info.title: Bronchiectasis
info.text: Imaging clue: thick-walled airways wider than the arteries beside them, with years of foul, purulent sputum.

info.title: Paragonimus westermani
info.text: Microscope clue: a golden-brown egg with a lid (operculum), after a meal of raw freshwater crab.

info.title: Tuberculosis
info.text: Imaging clue: an upper-lobe opacity in a patient with night sweats and weight loss.

info.title: Neurocysticercosis
info.text: Imaging clue: dozens of small cysts scattered through the brain of a patient with new seizures.

info.title: Caseous necrosis
info.text: Gross clue: a soft, crumbly, pale yellow-white center inside a lung lesion.

info.title: Emphysema
info.text: Gross clue: a smoker's lung with many enlarged, empty air spaces in the upper lobe.
